title: GitHub - mrscraper-com/mrscraper-mcp
snippet:
MrScraper MCP is the official [MrScraper](https://mrscraper.com) server for the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). It connects AI assistants to page content and Google search through two SDK-compatible tools, plus an account check. Retrieve HTML, Markdown, or screenshots with `scraperAPI`, discover pages with `webSearch`, and check your plan and token usage with `status`.
Use the hosted server with OAuth sign-in, or run the open-source server locally with the [`@mrscraper/mcp` npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mrscraper/mcp). See the [MrScraper MCP documentation](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server) for setup instructions and client configurations.
The server exposes three tools:
```
scraperAPI  webSearch  status
```
## Deployment options
| Option | Endpoint or command | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Hosted | `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` | A managed Streamable HTTP connection |
| Local HTTP | `TRANSPORT=http npx -y @mrscraper/mcp@latest` | A self-managed HTTP service |
| Local stdio | `npx -y @mrscraper/mcp@latest` | MCP clients that launch a local process |
The hosted server signs you in through your browser with OAuth 2.1, so there is no key to copy. Self-hosted and stdio setups use a MrScraper API key from [app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens](https://app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens), which the hosted server also still accepts.
## Connect to the hosted server
Point your MCP client at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` with no credential. The server answers with an OAuth challenge, your client opens a browser, and you approve the connection on `app.mrscraper.com`.
```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user \
mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
For clients configured by file, omit the `headers` block entirely:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"mrscraper": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
}
}
}
```
Use exactly this URL, including the `/mcp` path. It is the resource identifier access tokens are issued for, and a token minted for a different spelling of the address will be refused.

### Connect with an API key instead
An API key still works as a bearer token, which is what self-hosted deployments and non-OAuth clients use:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"mrscraper": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
"headers": {
"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
}
}
}
}
```
Use your client's environment-variable or secret-storage feature so the key stays out of project files.

# MCP Server
Access MrScraper’s web scraping API via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to enable AI agents to fetch and extract web data securely.
Use MrScraper’s web scraping API through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to let AI agents discover, fetch, and extract web data in real time. This cloud-hosted MCP server integrates directly with MrScraper, enabling secure, scalable scraping workflows without local setup or infrastructure management.
## Features
### AI Scraping
### Geo Unblocker
### Scraper Execution
### Bulk Scraping
### Results Management
### Rotating Proxies
### Cloud MCP Server
## Installation
### Prerequisites
To use the MrScraper MCP server, you'll need:
1. [A MrScraper account](https://v3.app.mrscraper.com/auth/login)
2. [MrScraper Account API Key](/docs/getting-started/api-token#generating-an-api-token)
### Remote Hosted URL via HTTP Transport Protocol
The simplest way to use MrScraper MCP is through our remotely hosted server. No local installation required!
Note

title: hermes-agent/optional-mcps/mrscraper/manifest.yaml at b79e8e12ee1819bbbe4061439cf379853c505c28 · NousResearch/hermes-agent
snippet:
manifest.yaml
# Nous-approved MCP catalog entry.
# Presence in this directory = approval. Merged via PR review.
manifest_version: 1
name: mrscraper
description: Retrieve web pages, search Google, and check account usage.
source: https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server
# Official hosted Streamable HTTP server. Its 401 challenge advertises MCP
# protected-resource metadata and an OAuth authorization server with dynamic
# client registration and PKCE. No local package or static key is required.
transport:
type: http
url: https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
auth:
type: oauth
# The server currently exposes scraperAPI, webSearch, and status.
# With no fixed tool filter, installation lets
# users choose among the tools available at connection time.
suggest:
keywords:
- mrscraper
- mr scraper
hosts:
- mrscraper.com
post_install: |
On first connection, Hermes opens MrScraper browser sign-in. Approve access
and start a new session to load its tools. If sign-in does not start, run:
hermes mcp login mrscraper
The server provides scraperAPI (HTML, Markdown, or screenshots),
webSearch (Google results), and status (account usage and quota).
For managed scrapers, reruns, and stored results, use the MrScraper dashboard.
Review or change enabled tools with:
hermes mcp configure mrscraper
Requests send target URLs and search queries to
MrScraper's cloud service. Scraping and search can consume account tokens;
use status to inspect your remaining quota before large jobs.

title: Use MrScraper MCP to Compare Public SaaS Pricing and Plan Limits
snippet:
An MCP SaaS pricing comparison uses an AI client, such as Claude Code, to collect official pricing and help pages through MrScraper's MCP tools. The client then turns each page into structured, cited rows. You compare plans only where units match, and you mark every unpublished price or limit as unknown.
**TL;DR**
- Start with one research question and a short list of comparable plans, then collect only official pricing pages, limit docs and FAQs.
- Store every fact as its own row with value, unit, billing period, source URL and observed date.
- Compare like with like. Seats, credits and fair-use wording stay separate unless the sources prove they match.
## **How does MCP SaaS pricing comparison work?**
It works in four steps: you define the question, MrScraper MCP collects the official pages, your AI client extracts facts into a fixed schema, and you build the comparison from those facts. MCP handles collection. The comparison rules are yours, and they live in your prompt and your review.

> "On October 23, 2026, what does the entry paid plan of Kit, MailerLite and Brevo cost per month for a list of 1,000 subscribers, and what sending, seat, automation and support limits come with it?"
That is the question we tested for this guide. It sets three things up front:
- **Scope:** three named email marketing tools and one plan each: Kit Creator, MailerLite Comfort and Brevo Starter.
- **Buyer:** a list of 1,000 subscribers, so prices that depend on list size can be read at the same tier.
- **Date:** one observation date for every row.

Collect the vendor's own pages: the pricing page first, then the help or documentation pages that define limits, then the pricing FAQ. Third-party review sites and old blog posts are often out of date, so use them only to find official pages, not as evidence.

Connect MrScraper's hosted MCP server to your AI client, then ask the client to call `scraperAPI` on each approved URL and extract facts into your schema. Each call returns the page content in the same response. Check the response before you trust any fact taken from it.
### **scraperAPI output and response validation**
MrScraper documents a hosted MCP endpoint at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` with OAuth 2.1 sign-in. In Claude Code, add it like this:
bash
```bash
claude mcp add \
--transport http \
--scope user \
mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
Open `/mcp` in Claude Code to sign in. Other clients, including Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code, use the same URL.
